text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Security forces kill 28 "terrorists" in Algiers, Chlef and Ain Defla.
- "Terrorists" families have been killed by rival factions.
- More than 7,000 export-import firms had been formed since 1993 when the Central Bank made the dinar currency convertible for foreign trade.
- The National Transitional Council pursues debate on poll legislation.
- Workers' Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA) named Sidi Said as acting secretary general to replace slain Abdelhak Benhamouda.
- President Liamine Zeroual invites party leaders for talks on elections, proving his willingness to end the transitional ruling period without elected parliament.
- The welfare system posts 57 billion dinars ($1 billion) deficit.
